note: R19 balance pass off tools/sim-emberveil.mjs (300 seeded runs, seed 1). The game had become easy: 28% of runs cleared all six acts, act 1 never failed once, and by act 4 an ordinary fight cost the party 2% of its health bar. The root cause was the XP curve — the party hit the level cap in act 5 and finished act 6 holding three times the XP the table asks for, so heroes outgrew every enemy multiplier. This pass stretches the XP table (progression.xpTable is now read by rules.js), trims the XP and gold multipliers, lifts the acts that had gone soft (1, 4, 6), gives enemies a per-act armour ramp and a little magic resist, makes bosses scale more like the trash around them, raises champion and named frequency with the act, and takes some of the shine off loot and crossings. Previous note (R14): act 2 was the wall — softened act 2, smoothed the act-2->3 HP step, lifted hero skill damage, and tuned hunger and torches. NG+ Act 1 uses the highest-act enemy multipliers (enemyScalingForNgPlus shifts effectiveAct = min(10, act + 4*ng)).

progression.note: R19: the table now runs to level 30 (it stopped at 20 here and rules.js carried its own copy ending at 38,160) and climbs much faster after level 10 — level 30 is 110,000 XP. Before the pass a party held 117k XP at the head of act 6 against a 38k cap, so it was level 30 with two acts still to play and enemies scaled for a much smaller party. statPointsPerLevel and passivePointEveryNLevels are NOT read from here yet — js/main.js hardcodes +2 attributes and every 5th level — so changing them would split the live game from the simulator. xpTable and talentPointLevels are live.

skill.note: M399: per-category split (heavy/light/magic). magicMult 0.78 brings spell damage about 22% under their pre-split numbers so spells stop dealing 4x basic-attack damage; bumping heroDamageMult 0.82 -> 0.95 keeps melee/ranged where they were after the M382 solo-viability fix, since the magic-only nerf carries the spell-rebalance load now.

mitigation.note: M207: both live + simulator run the WoW-style curve DR. DR = min(cap, armor/(armor+k)).

globalMultipliers.note: R19: unchanged. The per-act table below carries the difficulty now, and `armor` here is multiplied by the per-act `armor` figure.

actMultipliers.note: Per act: HP and damage multipliers, an armour multiplier applied on top of globalMultipliers.armor, and a flat magic-resist top-up (almost every enemy template has 0 magic resist and two thirds of hero damage is skills). Act 1's HP multiplier being higher than act 2's is not a mistake — these scale each act's own templates, and act-1 monsters have a fraction of the base HP act-2 monsters do.

ngPlus.note: M382: hpBase 1.35→2.5 and dmgBase 1.25→1.7 so NG+1 Act 1 actually feels like late-game combat. Combined with the act-shift (NG+1 Act 1 uses Act 5's actMultiplier), enemy effective HP is roughly Act 5 baseline × 2.5 in NG+1.

boss.note: A boss's HP multiplier is 1 + (actHpMult - 1) * hpShare, so it scales more gently than the trash around it. hpShare was hardcoded at 0.35 in rules.js makeEnemy; at act 6 that made a boss scale 1.65x while a trash mob scaled 2.85x. 0.5 keeps bosses a step behind the curve without making them a speed bump.

champion.note: Chance is `chance + perAct * (act - 1)`, so champions go from 1 in 20 in act 1 to 1 in 10 in act 6.

named.note: How often an ordinary node turns into a named leader with followers, and how much stronger that leader is.

partySize.note: M382: enemy damage scales with party size so a solo run isn't four-times harder than a four-hero run. Companions are NOT counted toward party size for this lookup — only heroes.

companions.note: M380: companions gain these attribute bonuses per (effective level − template level). Pairs with Companion Level Sync so an L1 War Dog hired in Act 1 actually scales into late game.

globalMultipliers.note: R20: xp 2.85 -> 2.2 — every zone gained a settlement this round (there is no fast travel any more, so the party has to be able to walk to a cleric), which keeps runs alive far longer and pushed fights per run from ~55 to ~95; at 2.85 the party held 237% of the XP its level asks for by act 6 and hit the level cap in act 5, the exact fault round 19 fixed. R19: xp 3 -> 2.85 and gold 1.2 -> 1.1 (both were hardcoded in game.js victory()). shopPrice marks up what a merchant asks without changing what he pays you for your leftovers (loot.sellPrice divides it back out); dropRate scales every zone drop.

loot.note: R19: affixMult scales every rolled affix value (items.json keeps the ranges); setChance is the per-kill chance of a set piece (was hardcoded 0.03 in loot.js); uniqueChance scales the per-boss unique odds in items.json bossLoot.

affixes.note: existing affix ranges are in src/game/items.js per-act tables (AFFIXES_ACT1..AFFIXES_ACT5). Baseline leaves these in code; tuning knobs in economy/enemies sections cover the target range for M4.

curveDr.note: Shipped in M207 via combat.mitigation.curveDr + liveFormula='curve-dr'.

world.note: Round 20: the travel layer Emberveil 2 added is tunable from here (js/game.js reads it). Night raids are the main risk of sleeping on the road.

nightRaid.note: A night raid is harder than the same fight in daylight (extra = extra bodies on top of the vehicle modifier, hp/damage multiply the raiders) and pays more (xp/gold multiply the win, dropChance is an extra roll on the zone drop table).
